title: Younium subscription billing (API v2): accounts, products with charge plans and charges, subscriptions with their versions and charges, sales orders, invoices with lines, payments, and the account's link to its Salesforce Account
status_note: Written on 1 November 2026 after what is publicly known of Younium's API v2 and its Salesforce connector, in our own words. The source pages could not be opened from the session that wrote the pack (developer.younium.com and support.younium.com are outside its allowed network), so every claim in this module is unverified until someone opens the pages: docs/YOUNIUM-SALESFORCE.md lists what to check. Nothing comes from a Younium tenant or a customer; validate_plan checks the pack against your rows. The table names are the API v2 resources in snake case (ACCOUNTS, SUBSCRIPTIONS, INVOICE_LINES); how a given pipeline names them in Fabric is the integrator's choice, and a system prefix (younium_) is read past.

variants.api_v2: Younium API v2 objects as the public API reference describes them (api-version 2.0/2.1), landed one table per resource with nested arrays (invoiceLines, versions, charges) as tables of their own. Not verified against any tenant.

younium_product_structure.title: Younium support: Younium's product structure (products, charge plans, charges; charge types Recurring, One-off, Usage, Measured; price period)
younium_product_structure.note: Unverified: not reachable from the writing session (1 November 2026). A web search result of that day quoting the article: products contain charge plans, charge plans contain charges; a charge sets the invoice description, its type, its price model, the price and the period the price applies to; charge types are Recurring, One-off, Usage and Measured; the price period matters for usage and measured charges whose billing period differs from it.

tables.name: ACCOUNTS
tables.en: Younium accounts (the customers that are billed)
tables.note: ID is a GUID; ACCOUNT_NUMBER is the number people use. EXTERNAL_CRM_ID holds the Salesforce Account Id when the Salesforce connector created or linked the account (a fixed mapping); EXTERNAL_ERP_ID the account's id in the ERP. CURRENCY is the account's currency: amounts of its subscriptions and invoices are in it. Field names after the API's camelCase (accountNumber, externalCrmId): a landing in snake case is read the same.

tables.name: PRODUCTS
tables.en: Products (what is sold; each has one or more charge plans)
tables.sv: Produkter (det som säljs; var och en har en eller flera avgiftsplaner)
tables.note: A product carries no price: prices sit on the charges of its charge plans.

tables.name: CHARGE_PLANS
tables.en: Charge plans (a way of pricing a product; one product, several plans)
tables.sv: Avgiftsplaner (ett sätt att prissätta en produkt)
tables.note: Nested under the product in the API (products[].chargePlans[]); landed as its own table it needs the product's id.

tables.name: CHARGES
tables.en: Charges of a charge plan (the items an account is charged for: recurring, one-off, usage, measured)
tables.sv: Avgifter i en avgiftsplan (det kontot debiteras för)
tables.note: CHARGE_TYPE is Recurring, One-off, Usage or Measured; the price is a list price per PRICE_PERIOD and not an amount: what an account pays is on SUBSCRIPTION_CHARGES, what it was billed on INVOICE_LINES. Usage and measured charges take their quantity from usage records, not from the subscription.

tables.name: SUBSCRIPTIONS
tables.en: Subscriptions (orders): one row per subscription number, with the account and the invoice account
tables.note: The API calls the number orderNumber. ACCOUNT_ID is the account the subscription belongs to, INVOICE_ACCOUNT_ID the account that receives the invoices; they can differ. A subscription carries no amount: its charges and quantities sit on the version valid for a period (SUBSCRIPTION_VERSIONS, SUBSCRIPTION_CHARGES). Whether a landing has one row per subscription or one row per version is the integrator's choice: in the API every version is returned with the subscription's number, so a table with the version's id as key is SUBSCRIPTION_VERSIONS below.

tables.name: SUBSCRIPTION_VERSIONS
tables.en: Subscription versions: every activated change to a subscription is a new version with its own effective period
tables.sv: Prenumerationsversioner: varje aktiverad ändring är en ny version med egen giltighetsperiod
tables.note: VERSION counts up; IS_LAST_VERSION marks the newest; EFFECTIVE_START_DATE and EFFECTIVE_END_DATE bound the period the version holds for. One version is valid on a given date. A measure that sums over all versions of a subscription (seats, recurring price) counts every change again; take the version valid on the date, or the last version.

tables.name: SUBSCRIPTION_CHARGES
tables.en: Charges on a subscription version (the agreed price and quantity per charge, per version)
tables.sv: Avgifter på en prenumerationsversion (avtalat pris och antal per avgift och version)

amounts.currency: the subscription's currency (SUBSCRIPTIONS.CURRENCY when the landing has it, otherwise the account's CURRENCY)

quantities.unit: the charge's unit; for usage and measured charges the quantity comes from usage, not from here

tables.note: Nested in the API under the version's products (products[].charges[]); the pack reads it as one table with the version's id and the catalog charge's id. PRICE is the agreed price per price period for this version: the recurring revenue of a subscription on a date is the sum over the charges of the one version valid on that date, recurring charges only, normalized to a month or a year (MRR, ARR). Summing PRICE over all versions is wrong by the number of versions.

tables.name: SALES_ORDERS
tables.en: Sales orders (the document that creates or changes a subscription)
tables.sv: Försäljningsordrar (dokumentet som skapar eller ändrar en prenumeration)
tables.note: Listed from the API's resource list; its fields and how it points at the subscription it created could not be read: unverified.

tables.name: INVOICES
tables.en: Invoices: header per invoice, with the account, the status (draft or posted) and the totals
tables.sv: Fakturor: en rad per faktura med konto, status (utkast eller bokförd) och summor
tables.note: TOTAL_AMOUNT is the whole invoice; a join with INVOICE_LINES repeats it once per line (the check 'the total that doubles'). STATUS tells a draft from a posted invoice: drafts can still change and need not carry a final number; billed revenue is the posted invoices.

tables.name: INVOICE_LINES
tables.en: Invoice lines (one per charge billed for a service period)
tables.note: Nested under the invoice in the API (invoiceLines[]). A line names what it bills by number: CHARGE_NUMBER, PRODUCT_NUMBER and the subscription's number; which of these the line carries, and under which names, could not be read, so those links are listed and not applied. SERVICE_PERIOD_START_DATE and SERVICE_PERIOD_END_DATE say what period the line bills.

tables.name: PAYMENTS
tables.note: A payment settles an open invoice (POST /Payments in API 2.1). Whether one payment can settle several invoices, and then lands as several rows or with a link table, could not be read: the link to the invoice is applied as many-to-one and must be confirmed with validate_plan.

relationships.condition: Holds for accounts the Salesforce connector created or linked: External CRM Id is filled from the Salesforce Account Id and cannot be mapped otherwise. Accounts created in Younium alone have no value (NULL, not an orphan). Salesforce shows ids with 15 characters and returns 18 through the API; a 15-character value finds nothing against an 18-character ACCOUNT.ID.

The subscription carries an externalCRMId; whether the connector fills it with the Opportunity Id of the opportunity that created the subscription could not be read. Listed, not applied: confirm it against your rows.
A sales order creates or changes a subscription; whether it carries the subscription's number could not be read. Listed, not applied.

The line bills one charge and is said to name it by its number; the field's presence and name could not be read. Listed, not applied: confirm it, or read it through the version's SUBSCRIPTION_CHARGES.
The line is said to name the subscription (orderNumber) it bills; the field's presence and name could not be read. Listed, not applied.
The line is said to name the product billed; the field's presence and name could not be read. Listed, not applied.
Applied as one invoice per payment row; a payment that settles several invoices would land otherwise (unverified). validate_plan's orphans and 'several' counts tell.

traps.title: Never sum over all versions of a subscription
traps.text: Every activated change to a subscription is a new version with its own effective period; the earlier version is closed with an end date. On any date exactly one version holds. A count of seats or a sum of recurring prices over SUBSCRIPTION_VERSIONS or SUBSCRIPTION_CHARGES without a date filter counts every change again. Take the version valid on the date (EFFECTIVE_START_DATE <= date < EFFECTIVE_END_DATE, or IS_LAST_VERSION for today).

traps.title: Amounts sit on charges and invoice lines, not on the subscription
traps.text: A subscription row carries no amount. What an account pays is PRICE and QUANTITY on SUBSCRIPTION_CHARGES of a version; what it was billed is AMOUNT on INVOICE_LINES, and TOTAL_AMOUNT on INVOICES is their sum: joined with its lines the header total is repeated once per line (the check 'the total that doubles').

traps.title: MRR and ARR are calculated measures, not columns
traps.text: Younium shows MRR, ARR and churn in its own reports; the API objects carry prices per price period, quantities and dates, not MRR. In Fabric they are measures: the recurring charges (CHARGE_TYPE Recurring) of the version valid on the date, PRICE times QUANTITY normalized to a month (MRR) or a year (ARR), in the account's currency. One-off, usage and measured charges are not recurring revenue; whether a measure includes them is a decision to write down, and the result will not equal Younium's own figure unless the definition is the same.

traps.title: One currency per account
traps.text: Amounts are in the account's currency (ACCOUNTS.CURRENCY, repeated on INVOICES.CURRENCY). A sum over several accounts without a conversion adds currencies. On the Salesforce side Opportunity.Amount is in CurrencyIsoCode only when the org has multi-currency enabled; otherwise there is no currency column and the amount is in the org's corporate currency.

traps.title: Usage and measured charges: the volume is separate
traps.text: A usage or measured charge is billed on a quantity reported as usage for the period, not on a quantity agreed on the subscription; its price may be per a price period that differs from the billing period. Keep the usage volume as its own measure and do not add usage lines into recurring revenue.

traps.title: Salesforce ids: 15 characters in the user interface, 18 through the API
traps.text: A Salesforce record id has 15 case-sensitive characters; the API and most exports give the 18-character case-safe form, whose first 15 characters are the same. ACCOUNTS.EXTERNAL_CRM_ID is filled by the connector (18 characters) but an id typed or pasted from the user interface has 15: a join finds nothing for that row, and a case-insensitive database may pair two different 15-character ids. Compare on 18 characters (CASESAFEID in Salesforce), never on the first 15 alone.

traps.title: One customer, two account rows
traps.text: The same customer is a Salesforce Account (ACCOUNT, key ID) and a Younium account (ACCOUNTS, key ID, with ACCOUNT_NUMBER). Only ACCOUNTS.EXTERNAL_CRM_ID = ACCOUNT.ID binds them; a match on the name is not the link, and an account created in Younium alone has no Salesforce row. A subscription also has an invoice account that can differ from its account: bill-to and sold-to can be two rows.

traps.title: Fields without a value are left out of the API's JSON
traps.text: The API omits a field that has no value rather than sending null. A landing that infers its columns from the JSON of one load can lack a column (EXTERNAL_CRM_ID, EFFECTIVE_END_DATE) that the next load has: fix the column list from the reference, not from a sample.

traps.title: Draft and posted invoices
traps.text: An invoice is a draft first and posted afterwards. Drafts can change and are not billed revenue; a sum over INVOICES without STATUS = posted counts them.

traps.title: The table names are the integrator's choice
traps.text: Younium has no fixed table names in Fabric: a pipeline over the API names its tables. The pack knows the API's resource names in snake case (SUBSCRIPTION_VERSIONS for the versions array, INVOICE_LINES for invoiceLines) and reads camelCase and snake_case columns alike, and a system prefix (younium_) is read past; a landing that names them otherwise is matched by the name rules alone.
